An Elegant Dining Experience at Reflections – Caravelle Saigon
Oct 2026 • Couples
We had a lovely evening at Reflections Restaurant, located in the iconic Caravelle Saigon Hotel, overlooking the historic Saigon Opera House.

I had specifically requested a window table overlooking the Opera House when making our reservation, and we were delighted that the restaurant accommodated our request. As luck would have it, we were seated at the very table featured in many of the restaurant’s promotional photographs. With its elegant setting, tasteful floral arrangements and splendid nighttime views, it was certainly a wonderful spot for dinner.

A particularly thoughtful touch was the personalised handwritten welcome note from the restaurant manager, which made us feel genuinely welcomed.

The food was beautifully presented, with considerable attention paid to the plating and finer details. For our main course, we decided to share the Kagoshima A5 Wagyu beef, as neither of us consumes much beef these days. The Wagyu was excellent, as one would expect from beef of this calibre — rich, flavourful and beautifully prepared. An interesting touch was the selection of different salts provided to complement the beef, allowing us to experiment with the various flavours. The Prosecco and Pinot Noir we enjoyed during dinner were also very good and complemented the meal nicely.

Our server, Ms Dieu, was professional, attentive and accommodating throughout the evening. She kindly helped convey our request to share the Wagyu to the kitchen and generally took very good care of us.

There was a slight mix-up in the sequencing of our earlier courses, with my appetiser arriving alongside my soup while my wife’s appetiser came a little later. A minor hiccup, but it certainly did not detract significantly from an otherwise enjoyable evening.

Overall, Reflections offers a refined and intimate dining experience, combining elegant surroundings, beautifully prepared cuisine and warm, professional hospitality. The lovely views of the Opera House, thoughtful personal touches and excellent Wagyu made it a memorable evening in Ho Chi Minh City. A special mention to Ms Dieu for her attentive service.

We had high hopes for this restaurant based on reviews, but found it average and over priced. The restaurant is spacious and well laid out, the decor is a little dated but tasteful and classic. Tables are beautifully set and there are lovely thoughtful touches of welcome cards and small gifts… all in all it sets high expectations from the outset. Service is not especially assured, you are set to expect polished fine dining service, but what you get misses the mark more than often. Waiters hover and remove plates from diners while others are still eating, multiple times per course.. and I could hear and see them scrapping dinners in the service areas from my seat. Salt and pepper is left on the table for dessert… all small things, but impacted on the experience. The food itself was well presented, but soulless and lacking in real flavour. The passion fruit sorbet I ordered to finish was icy and tasteless. We enjoyed the atmosphere but the food was average for the price point and asking for the bill appears to trigger complex arrangements of financial calculations and signatures (we serve staying in house). We had a much better experience for around the same price at Anan Saigon… different concept, but the food and service were exceptional. All in all, I’d avoid… if you love fine dining with all the trappings, Reflections will likely disappoint. ☹️

One of South East Asia's top dining experiences
Dec 2023 • Family
It's rare to stumble across a restaurant that drops in to your "top X" restaurants, but after my meal at Reflections in December 2023 I left with a personal wow moment, I was so happy to have eaten here and enjoyed the unbelievable food.
The restaurant definitely has a slightly older feel to it, the tables and chairs and the ambience make the feeling of this restaurant a little edgy, but it's definitely clean and that's most important.
Staff here are great. Simple things like recommendations for coffee, tea, all of which added a lot of value to our evening.
As for the food - the attention to detail that went into each dish blew my mind. Very rare is it to have a dish that leaves the hairs on your arms tingling, when you realise that the dish is absolute perfection, flawless and the combination of flavours has all come together. I was so impressed. For starters, we had Roasted organic beetroot and beef tomato with toasted hazelnuts, Burrata and basil coulis and spring rolls. 10/10 for each. The chicory aIberico pork collar was the jewel in the crown, so delicious. Having said that, the cod fish filet with kabu, salmon roe and Bottarga came in a close second, it feels almost unfair to give the win to the pork collar.... 
I hope that the feedback that I gave to the staff made it back to the kitchen team. If it didn't, @ Head Chef on Sun Dec 17 - keep up the stunning work!
Can't wait to return.

It's not often that I get to enjoy dinner here, so I had high hopes. While the 3-course meal was alright, the main course was slightly disappointing. It was spice and chicory Iberico pork collar with glaze Portobello and apple gel. The flavour was great, there was a good contrast between the savoury and the sour tastes, between the soft and firm textures, but the problem was that the portion was too little - three small cuts of pork. It didn't come off as a main course, so it really set the experience back.

But otherwise, everything else was fine. Service was good, the other two dishes were pretty delicious, the atmosphere was relaxing and there was live music. 7.5/10.

Excellent meal and service in a wonderful setting
Mar 2014 • Friends
This was quite a meal in Ho Chi Minh City. Reflections is a beautiful place on the third floor of the Caravelle Hotel in the heart of the city. This is the famous hotel where all the Western journalists stayed during the Viet Nam War also being the most luxurious hotel in the city at the time. Fast forward to today, and it is still a beautiful place centrally located, the original 9 story building has been preserved and updated and a beautiful new tower with a Las Vegas-type lobby was erected next to it. First we went to the old 9th floor open-air terrace for a drink overlooking the city lights, the busy streets and the beautiful Belle Époque Opera House across the street. If was a balmy night but the breezes kept us cool. After our drink we went down to Reflections Restaurant on the third floor. This is a very beautiful place overlooking the same Opera House and streets but from a much lower angle. We were lucky to secure a window table which made the experience even better. The place is dimly lighted which made the experience even nicer. Our the table had a glass top with beautiful arrangement of fresh flowers.
We were given the menus and chose the 3 course fixed-price dinner (798,000 Viet Dongs) which was really a good deal since one can order anything in the menu with a few exceptions that carry a surcharge. The menu rivals any good French restaurant, my companion and I chose the identical same things to order (not very creative, I know). After we ordered they served a beautiful basket of assorted breads. We ordered the lobster appetizer, which carries a 120,000 Viet Dong surcharge each, and it was delicious served on a bed of braised leeks with wild mushrooms on a very delicate clear sauce. The main course was a poached fresh sea bass served with shrimp, cauliflower, broccoli, bay scallops and on top a light crab meat sauce, sounds like lot of things in one dish but they all blended together and tasted fresh. Then for dessert we opted on caramelized banana mille freuille, delicious. All excellent with excellent service and when we paid the bill was less than US$200, including a round of drinks and a large bottle of water. We looked at the wine list but we thought the prices were really high for what they were offering so we stuck to the drinks which were reasonable and all worked out very well. This is the kind of place that you can dine in either with business associates or on a date. I highly recommend it next time you are visiting Ho Chi Minh City.
